title: Best ALL – Accor Live Limitless hotels in Cambodia
intro: Cambodia is a small market with an unusually strong top end: {{count}} ALL - Accor Live Limitless hotels split between Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Sihanoukville, anchored by two colonial-era Raffles landmarks and two Sofitel Phokeethra resorts. Below them sit Novotel, TRIBE and ibis properties covering the mid and budget tiers.
editorial_notes: Hand-drafted 2026-08-31 as the second batch, after GSC showed the first five guides outperforming the 650+ hotel pages (two in the site's top 10; the top page site-wide over the preceding 7 days was a guide). Counts use the {{count}} placeholder resolved at build time by src/lib/listicles.js -- never hardcode a count here. City and brand names were read from data/entities at draft time; no figure is stated in prose that the placeholder does not cover. Deliberately omits the boilerplate "How is this list ranked?" FAQ the first batch carries: the guide template already states the ranking basis on-page, so repeating it on every guide would just duplicate content.

faqs.question: How many ALL - Accor Live Limitless hotels are there in Cambodia?
faqs.answer: EliteStay tracks {{count}} Accor-affiliated hotels in Cambodia, with most in Phnom Penh, several in Siem Reap near the Angkor temples, and one on the Sihanoukville coast. Accor is the best-represented of the four loyalty programmes this directory covers in Cambodia.

faqs.question: Which are the landmark Accor properties in Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Raffles Hotel Le Royal in Phnom Penh and Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor in Siem Reap are both restored colonial-era landmarks and among the highest-scoring hotels in this list, joined by the two Sofitel Phokeethra resorts in those same two cities.
